headline: Hurricanes reach one-year, $3M deal with Alexander Nikishin
take:
ESPN reports that the Hurricanes have agreed to a one-year, $3 million contract with restricted free agent defenseman Alexander Nikishin, ending a monthslong standoff. The deal comes about a month into the season, so he was missing from the start.

Carolina has not needed him to get here. The Hurricanes are 9-2-2 with 20 points through 13 games, and they have controlled play so far this season. Their share of expected goals, which measures the quality of chances each side creates, is 60.9 percent, and it sits at 59 percent at five-on-five. Their power play generates 0.92 expected goals per game, and their penalty kill allows 0.52. Goalie play has added a little on top, with goals saved above expected at 1, meaning the goalies have stopped about one more goal than the shots faced would predict. Results have run slightly below the chances, with goals minus expected at -0.4, so there is no sign of a lucky start. Nikishin joins a team that is already strong rather than one patching a hole, which makes this a depth addition to watch as he works into the lineup.
